mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 195) signals persistent price pressures, prompting central bank tightening expectations that depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 195.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month averages signals robust consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5%) indicates economic weakness, reducing corporate profit growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong job growth (PAYEMS) signals a healthy labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k.

mechanism_narrative: Weak industrial production (INDPRO < 115) indicates slowing economic activity, increasing recession risks and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO falls below 115.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month average and GDP growth (GDPC1) above its 4-quarter average signals robust economic expansion, boosting equity returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when both HOUST and GDPC1 exceed their respective 12-month and 4-quarter averages.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%.
